item.title: Richardson retires as basketball announcer
item.description: BROOKVILLE — The golden tones of Brookville Basketball Public Address Announcer Mark Richardson came to an end February 14 after 48 years behind the microphone. Richardson officially retired from the position following the Blue Devils game against Middletown Madison. The post Richardson retires as basketball announcer appeared first on The Register Herald.

item.title: Board hires new elementary principal
item.description: BROOKVILLE — The Brookville Local Schools Board of Education approved a three-year contract (225 days) for Josh Pohl, who will become the district’s new elementary school principal. The post Board hires new elementary principal appeared first on The Register Herald.

item.title: MVCAP Winter Crisis Program continues amid high demand
item.description: EATON — Brutal cold temperatures and rising utility rates have contributed to higher heating bills this winter, and the Miami Valley Community Action Partnership (MVCAP) is reporting increased demand for its Winter Crisis Program and other utility assistance services. item.title: PCHS to unveil Underground Railroad exhibit
item.description: EATON — The Preble County Historical Society will unveil a new exhibit highlighting the Underground Railroad in Preble County on Saturday, Feb. 28, in honor of Black History Month. The post PCHS to unveil Underground Railroad exhibit appeared first on The Register Herald.

item.title: Eaton grad nominated for an Oscar
item.description: LOS ANGELES, CALIFORNIA — Preble County residents preparing to watch the 2026 Oscars on Sunday, March 15, should add the short film “The Singers” to their must watch list. Nominated under the “Best Live-Action Short” category, “The Singers” was directed by Sam Davis and produced by Jack Piatt. item.title: Camden native overcomes medical crisis to become educator
item.description: CEDARVILLE — Brandon Stover woke up in a hospital after an 18-hour seizure and didn’t recognize his father. This spring, he will walk across Cedarville University’s commencement stage on his way to a career in special education.
